answer: A bonded unique-agent registry issues a rotating spiral challenge and a sparrow-coded attestation; agents lock stake and register a commitment, with rewards concave in stake and capped per epoch. Splitting stake across N identities yields sum f(s_i) ≤ f(sum s_i) under concavity, so no extra payout. Attackers pay locked stake, attestation/oracle fees, and slashing for duplicate commitments. This does not prove one bond equals one person; limitations include identity rental, collusion, and oracle compromise, so a voyage to full Sybil resistance remains incomplete.
